definition: The first required bet, placed before the cards are dealt. It wins or loses against the dealer's hand, but **pushes** if the dealer does not [[qualify]].
The second required bet, always equal to the [[Ante]]. It loses whenever you lose, but pays only when you win with a straight or better.
The one raise you are allowed per hand: **4×** or **3×** the Ante before the flop, **2×** after the flop, or **1×** after the river. It pays 1 to 1 and ignores whether the dealer qualifies.
An optional side bet on your own best five of seven cards. It pays for three of a kind or better, win or lose against the dealer, and even if you [[fold]].
The two private cards each player gets. You and the dealer each have two.
The five shared cards: three on the [[flop]], then the [[turn]] and [[river]] together. Also called the board.
The first three community cards. If you checked before the flop, you may bet **2×** here or [[check]] again.
The fourth community card. In UTH it is dealt together with the [[river]].
The fifth community card. If you checked twice, you must now bet **1×** or [[fold]].
The first decision, made after seeing only your two cards: **Bet 4x**, **Bet 3x** or **Check**.
Make no Play bet for now. It is free, and it lets you see the next cards. Checking is how you wait for more information.
Give up your [[Ante]] and [[Blind]] (exactly 2 Antes), and stop. You can only fold at the river, instead of betting 1×.
The moment both hands are turned over and compared. Your best five of seven cards against the dealer's.
The dealer qualifies with **a pair or better** (best five of seven). If not, the [[Ante]] pushes.
A bet that is returned to you unchanged: no win, no loss. Ties push everything.
Both hands rank exactly the same, five cards for five cards. The Ante, Blind and Play all [[push]]. Suits never break ties.
A leftover card used to break a tie between hands of the same kind. A pair of kings with an ace beats a pair of kings with a queen.
Your hand is the best five-card poker hand you can make from your two hole cards and the five community cards, using both, one or none of your own cards.
When the best five cards are all on the board, for both players. Neither hole card counts, and the hand is a tie.
The lowest straight, A-2-3-4-5. The ace counts low here. A straight cannot wrap around, so Q-K-A-2-3 is not a straight.
A pair that uses one of your hole cards: a pocket pair, or a hole card matching a board rank. A pair that sits on the board belongs to the dealer just as much as to you.
Two hole cards of the same rank, such as {{Qs Qd}}.
Two hole cards of the same suit. Written with an s, as in AKs.
Two hole cards of different suits. Written with an o, as in AKo.
One of the 169 distinct starting hands, ignoring exact suits: 13 pairs (77), 78 suited hands (AKs) and 78 offsuit hands (T9o).
On the river, the number of unseen cards that would give the dealer a better hand than yours. It decides the close river calls.
The average result of a decision if you could face the same spot millions of times. Short form: **EV**.
Short for [[expected value]]: the average result of a decision, measured here for the whole hand (Ante, Blind and Play together).
One Ante. EV is measured in Ante units, so "+1.17 antes" scales with your bet: at a $10 Ante it is $11.70.
The average share of each Ante the casino keeps in the long run with perfect play. Per hand, it is the expected loss divided by the Ante.
The expected loss divided by the total amount you put on the felt. It is smaller than the house edge per Ante, because it counts every Play bet.
The list of every option at a decision, with its average result for the whole hand, its cost against the best option and a tier badge.
The average amount a choice gives up compared with the best option. Also called regret. It is never called a house edge.
The badge for the option with the highest EV. Equal options both get it.
The tier for a choice that costs up to 0.02 antes against the best option.
The tier for a choice that costs up to 0.10 antes against the best option.
The tier for a choice that costs up to 0.50 antes against the best option. The EV sheet shows a better alternative.
The tier for a choice that costs more than 0.50 antes against the best option. It asks for a second tap before it goes through.
The list of what a bet pays for each hand. The Blind and Trips have their own paytables.
The play that gives the lowest possible house edge: the exact best option at every decision.
A practical strategy with a short chart: the preflop chart, a simple flop rule and a simple river rule. It costs only a little more than perfect play.
The lightest practical strategy, with easier preflop and flop rules at a slightly higher cost.
How far real results swing around the average. A good decision can lose, and a bad one can win, on any single hand.
The money you set aside for playing. It should cover many bad swings.
One sitting at the table, a number of hands played in a row.
A measure of the typical size of the swings in a single hand's result, in Antes.
An optional side bet that pays on the best five of six cards: your two hole cards plus four community cards. Tables vary.
An optional side bet that pays on your two hole cards plus the flop, with top prizes taken from a growing jackpot meter.
An optional side bet that pays when your hand loses at showdown with a big hand. Tables vary widely.
Quick-fire practice that deals one decision at a time and grades it against the exact best option.
